Alex — thanks for the clear asks. High-level answers below; I can follow up with a one-page decision record and an export checklist if you want.

1) Retention scope we can provide during a short forensic hold: 
   - Full request/response traces (application-level request body headers + model input metadata) — retained for 30 days in raw form on our forensic hold slice.
   - Inference-level token caches and intermediate KV blobs — retained for 7 days by default; can be extended to 30 days if you explicitly request the forensic export.
   - System access logs (load balancer, kube audit) — retained unredacted for 90 days in-region.

2) Residency: all held artifacts for this customer are kept in the US region for this account by default. We do NOT replicate the forensic hold slice to EU without an explicit signed request.

3) Handoff/export: we can produce a signed export bundle that includes: 
   - NDJSON of request/response traces (with agreed redaction rules), 
   - compressed system logs (gz), 
   - SHA256 checksums for each file, 
   - a short chain-of-custody manifest signed by a Redwood security engineer.

Next steps I propose: 
- You confirm whether Acme requires raw request bodies or a redacted variant.
- If raw, we will open a temporary forensic hold and create an export candidate.

I'll loop in Karthik for feasibility and Marissa for legal/retention policy confirmation.

Regards,
Naomi Feldman
Director, Customer Security — Redwood Inference

Quick technical notes on implementability and timeline: 

- We can create a per-account forensic slice within the US cluster within ~2 hours. That slice will be immutable for the hold duration and snapshot-exportable.
- For raw request bodies: storage contains sensitive tokens (if present). We will not export PII/PHI unless we have a written attestation from the customer allowing it; alternatively we can apply deterministic redaction rules (email/hash, SSN mask). 
- Export format: NDJSON + gz archive with per-file SHA256. Exports can be delivered to a signed S3 pre-signed URL in the customer's cloud or via encrypted transfer to an Acme-designated SFTP endpoint.
- Chain-of-custody: we will include a manifest with timestamps, the operator's name (Redwood engineer who generated the bundle), and the SHA256s. We can also seed the manifest with a notarized signature from our HSM if Acme requires higher assurance (legal asks).

Operational constraints: if you request raw bodies for 30 days, it will increase the forensic slice size and may trigger a temporary storage chargeback to the customer under our emergency export policy. I'll prepare an estimated size/cost once you confirm the time range.

-Karthik
Principal SRE — Redwood Inference

Naomi / team — legal guidance below (approved with conditions).

Decision and required controls:
1) Authorization: require a short written attestation from Acme specifically authorizing the export of raw request/response bodies that may contain PHI/PII. Use the following minimal wording in the attestation: 

"Acme Health authorizes Redwood Inference to export raw request and response artifacts associated with incident ACME-TKT-7712 for the purpose of forensic analysis. Acme confirms it has authority to receive PHI/PII and will handle the data in accordance with applicable law and its internal policies."

2) Retention window: approve 30-day forensic hold for raw artifacts on the condition that the attestation is received. If attestation is not received within 24 hours, proceed with redacted exports only. System audit logs retention (90 days) remains unchanged.

3) Chain-of-custody: require that the export manifest include operator identity, timestamp, SHA256 per-file, and storage destination. Redwood must retain an internal signed copy of the manifest for 2 years.

4) Delivery: prefer customer-managed S3 presigned URL if Acme can provide one with write access; otherwise use encrypted SFTP. Any export to a non-US destination requires an explicit cross-border approval (not the case here).

Naomi, Marissa: please confirm you will collect the attestation and attach it to the ticket. Karthik: once attestation is received, proceed with slice creation and export prep; include a cost estimate in the export bundle.

Approved-by: Stephanie Nguyen, Counsel — Redwood Inference
